title: Throughput accreditation manifest: tenant-aware harness, benchmark recipes, and customer acceptance kit
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Deliver a reproducible, customer-facing accreditation bundle that certifies Dedicated capacity throughput guarantees and autoscaler behavior for customer signoff. The bundle ("PulseForge Accreditation Manifest") includes: 1) a tenant-aware load driver and runner that replays production mixes and synthetic stress profiles, 2) a set of canonical benchmark recipes and pass/fail criteria tied to SLAs (throughput, p99/p99.9 latency, error rate), and 3) a customer acceptance checklist + handoff notebook for onboarding Dedicated customers.

Background: Customers buying Dedicated capacity want predictable throughput guarantees and deterministic autoscaling behavior. Current internal throughput docs and ad-hoc load runs lack a single reproducible artifact that ties load scripts, telemetry dashboards, and acceptance criteria together. This ticket builds that artifact and a corresponding CI-enabled validation flow.

Scope (in-scope):
- Build PulseForge runner: lightweight, multi-node driver that can orchestrate tenant mixes, tenant isolation testing, and KV cache priming. Supports replay from recorded traces and synthetic generators (ramp, steady, microburst).
- Define 6 benchmark recipes: baseline steady-state, tenant-mix-90/10, microburst-10s, autoscaler-churn, cold-start-warmup, and failure-fallback (model-variant degrade).
- Formalize pass/fail thresholds: sustained_rps, p99_ms, p99.9_ms, error_percent, autoscaler_scale_down_recovery_time.
- Customer acceptance playbook: step-by-step runbook, expected artifacts (telemetry links, run logs), and a signoff template.

Out-of-scope:
- Changes to the autoscaler control plane itself (separate ENG change request).
- Long-term synthetic dataset curation beyond initial 10 representative tenant traces.

Acceptance criteria:
- PulseForge runner is in repo with README and CI smoke test (runs in a small local mode). Link to PR created.
- All 6 benchmark recipes are executable and produce an HTML/JSON result summary that maps to the pass/fail thresholds.
- Customer acceptance kit packaged as a single Confluence page + a Colab/Notebook for replay. Confluence URL included in attachments.
- A run demonstrating sustained target throughput for a sample tenant mix (example: 12k RPS sustained over 30m with p99 < 120ms) with reproducible commands.

Architectural notes and design choices:
- Driver: Go-based controller that schedules workers, collects timeline-aligned telemetry, and writes normalized events. We prefer Go for low latency resource use and easy binary distribution for on-prem customers.
- Load generation: use a combination of native PulseForge generators (for precise KV priming and model variant switching) and wrk2 for raw RPS stress where microsecond timing fidelity is not required.
- Telemetry ingestion: tests push trace/metrics to an isolated test Prometheus + Loki stack; results pipeline emits per-run JSON and an HTML summary. CI will validate baseline results against a stored golden file for regressions.
- Autoscaler test: orchestrate step ramps and sustained loads; assert scale-up latency and stability windows. Add an intentional partial-failure scenario where one node is drained to exercise fallback routing.

Risks and mitigations:
- Noise from other infra tenants: use isolated test fleet or dedicated namespaces and tenant isolation flags to prevent contamination.
- Test runtime variability: standardize warmup cadence and sample window (discard first 5 minutes) to reduce noise.
- Customer data constraints for replay: use synthetic anonymized traces and a strict PII redaction step prior to replay when customers provide traces.

Deliverables:
- repo: github.com/redwood-inference/pulseforge (initial PR: PR-142)
- confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DC/PulseForge+Accreditation+Manifest
- acceptance checklist + example signoff document
- CI job: nightly accreditation run against a pinned test fleet

Operational follow-ups (post-merge):
- Run the manifest for the next two Dedicated onboards and collect lessons.
- Iterate recipes based on customer workloads and add an autoscaler SLO upgrade doc.
